Rebuilt H=J H0_prime−J_prime H0 symbolically from these formulas, independently extracted the 20 Fourier-Laurent terms with beta degree≤2 and frequency≤4, reproduced all 15 nonzero degree-20 Taylor coefficients from order 6, exact per-degree coefficient norms 14sqrt3+6sqrt7+2sqrt291+4sqrt111<117, 114 and 48, negative high-order Taylor mass 0.053565<0.06, and global exponential remainder coefficient 0.000170004<1/5000. Combining Q20>0.4 beta^6 with remainder<beta^6/5000 gives H>0 for every 0<beta≤pi/6, not just a sampled grid; U_prime>0. Endpoint derivatives give U(0+)=1/3 and U(pi/6)=(3+2sqrt3−2pi)/(2pi−6), hence derivative sign proves three sharp phases and uniqueness/nonattainment. value.rationale: Optimizing outer parallel area over the canonical regular r-disk triangle family at fixed minimum width is a natural intrinsic geometry/Pál-to-Blaschke-Lebesgue tradeoff: Steiner polynomial couples two classical competing invariants, area and perimeter. The theorem establishes exact sharp transition ratios (1/3,tau+), unique interior curved optimum on a genuine open interval, strict comparison to both endpoint shapes, and boundary uniqueness/nonattainment through a substantive global analytic curvature certificate. This is not just restatement of known scalar area/perimeter formulas or simple endpoint substitution; the precise variable-radius optimizer would be useful for geometric offset and width extremal studies. No claim of global optimality outside this family.
residual_risks: The classification is deliberately only within regular Euclidean disk triangles of fixed minimum width; the limiting equilateral is unattained for finite r.
The natural relevance is to this family and parallel geometry, not a demonstrated global minimization theorem for all ball-convex bodies.

limitations: Applies only to Euclidean planar regular r-disk triangles with fixed minimum width, outer circular offsets t≥0, r≥w; no optimum among arbitrary convex bodies or all r-ball convex sets.
Equilateral triangle occurs only in the r→infinity limit, so first phase has an infimum not a finite minimizer.
The exact symbolic/Fourier computation has an independently checked continuous-domain remainder argument, but is not a Lean or expert-attested formal proof.
Novelty is best-of-knowledge; area/perimeter formulas and Steiner polynomial itself are known and credited, and unindexed equivalent phase classifications cannot be ruled out.
Science complete; publication withheld for confidentiality clearance of public metadata/workflow provenance, not for mathematical reasons.
